stem: A heart transplant candidate on the waitlist develops worsening dyspnea. Which repeat evaluation study aligns with standard waitlist monitoring references?

options.text: Right heart catheterization to evaluate pulmonary pressures
Colonoscopy to calculate lung allocation score
Bone densitometry as the sole required cardiac study
No repeat cardiac testing is ever indicated while waitlisted

explanation.rationale_correct: Heart waitlist candidates undergo repeated testing to reevaluate health status, including right heart catheterization to evaluate pulmonary pressures when clinically indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Colonoscopy is a health-maintenance study, not a cardiac waitlist monitoring test for pulmonary pressures.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bone densitometry does not replace cardiac hemodynamic assessment on the heart waitlist.
rationale_incorrect.D: Repeat testing is performed as necessary to monitor candidacy and listing status.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Right heart catheterization to evaluate pulmonary pressures

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → heart transplant candidates → 4.b.i. (repeat right heart catheterization for pulmonary pressures); PDF p. 54 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 020100 item; heart waitlist hemodynamic monitoring distinct from positive stress-test referral (cctc-2033) and PELD rule (cctc-2010); anchor verified on Cupples p. 54.

stem: During liver transplant evaluation of a candidate with alcohol-related liver disease, which adherence measure may a center require per standard references?

options.text: A behavioral contract to abstain from alcohol with random toxicology screening
Continued daily alcohol use until the transplant operation
No documentation of abstinence is ever permitted

explanation.rationale_correct: Centers may require patients with alcohol-related liver disease to sign a behavioral contract indicating they will abstain from alcohol and undergo random toxicology screening to confirm ongoing abstinence.

rationale_incorrect.B: Candidates for liver transplantation are expected to remain abstinent rather than continue alcohol use.
rationale_incorrect.C: Formal rehabilitation or Alcoholics Anonymous participation may be required depending on center protocol and patient suitability.
rationale_incorrect.D: Abstinence assessment and behavioral contracts are common components of alcohol screening.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Evaluation → e. Alcohol screening → v.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: behavioral contract indicating that they will abstain from alcohol and undergo random toxicology screening

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → e. Alcohol screening → v. (behavioral contract and random toxicology screening for ongoing abstinence); PDF p. 43 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Tenth 020300 item; liver alcohol-contract angle distinct from PAK (cctc-2050), transition (cctc-2056), and indeterminate outcome (cctc-2035); anchor verified on Cupples p. 43.

stem: A pulmonologist refers a patient with advanced lung disease for transplant evaluation. Which referral-timing consideration aligns with standard lung evaluation references?

options.text: Late referral when the patient is too sick may preclude transplantation
Referral timing has no effect on transplant candidacy
Only patients already on mechanical ventilation at referral are acceptable candidates
Early referral is contraindicated for all lung disease

explanation.rationale_correct: Timing of referral is a key aspect of lung transplantation; referrals late in the disease process may result in the patient being too sick for transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Referral timing directly affects whether the patient remains a suitable transplant candidate.
rationale_incorrect.C: Late referral leading to excessive illness is the concern described, not a requirement for pre-referral ventilation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Appropriately timed early referral is encouraged rather than contraindicated for all patients.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Referrals that are late in the disease process may result in the patient being too sick for transplantation

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 11 → Patient Referral → 3.a. (late referral may leave patient too sick for transplant); PDF p. 567 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eleventh 020300 item; lung referral-timing angle distinct from pulmonary rehab requirement (cctc-2034) and LAS reporting (cctc-2044); anchor verified on Cupples p. 567.

stem: A kidney transplant candidate has a history of prior graft or shunt thrombosis. Which preoperative coordination step aligns with standard evaluation references?

options.text: Screen for hypercoagulability with tests such as activated protein C resistance and antiphospholipid studies
Omit all coagulation testing because thrombosis history is irrelevant
Proceed without evaluation because hypercoagulability cannot be assessed
Cancel transplantation permanently for any prior clot without further workup

explanation.rationale_correct: Kidney preoperative evaluation includes hypercoagulability screening for patients with a history of graft or shunt thrombosis, including tests such as activated protein C resistance, factor V and prothrombin mutations, and antiphospholipid antibodies.

rationale_incorrect.B: Thrombosis history triggers additional preoperative coagulation evaluation rather than being ignored.
rationale_incorrect.C: Standard references list specific hypercoagulability tests for at-risk candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Thrombosis history prompts evaluation and risk mitigation rather than automatic permanent cancellation without assessment.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: history of grafts or shunt thrombosis should be screened for hypercoagulability

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → kidney preoperative evaluation → 5.a.ii. (hypercoagulability screening after graft/shunt thrombosis history); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 020700 item; kidney hypercoagulability screening distinct from urine baseline (cctc-2016), liver MELD removal data (cctc-2044), and cardiac stress testing (cctc-2028); anchor verified on Cupples p. 46.
